title: Mark Type Symbol Set
purpose: Define a unique symbolic legend for marks of honour, marks of distinction, marks of valour, marks of identity, and demerits without reusing symbols from the 17D symbolic set.

core_definition.summary: This UKR assigns five unique symbols to five different kinds of marks. Each symbol functions as a stable visual anchor for a specific mark category. The symbol identifies the category but does not replace evidence, context, issuing authority, or the person's full identity.
core_definition.governing_rule: A mark points to a category of recognition, identification, or penalty; it does not become total proof of the whole person.

core_separation.false_equation: mark = total identity or automatic proof
core_separation.corrected_equation: mark = category_signal + context + issuing_authority + reason + evidence_boundary
core_separation.one_line_translation: A mark points to something; it does not become the whole person.

symbol_set.plain_translation: This marks honour or respected conduct.
symbol_set.boundary: A mark of honour recognizes honourable conduct, but it does not prove superiority over others.

symbol_set.meaning_lock: notable difference, recognized excellence, standing apart
symbol_set.plain_translation: This marks someone or something as distinct from the ordinary set.
symbol_set.boundary: A mark of distinction proves difference or recognition, but not automatic moral goodness.

symbol_set.meaning_lock: courage under risk, pressure, danger, or conflict
symbol_set.plain_translation: This marks courage under danger or serious pressure.
symbol_set.boundary: A mark of valour recognizes bravery in context, but it does not mean the person is perfect in all contexts.

symbol_set.meaning_lock: identification, role, belonging, signature, personal marker
symbol_set.plain_translation: This identifies who, what, where, or which role something belongs to.
symbol_set.boundary: A mark of identity identifies; it does not automatically prove merit, guilt, ownership, honour, or authority.

symbol_set.meaning_lock: penalty, fault, negative mark, misconduct record
symbol_set.plain_translation: This marks a negative record, penalty, fault, or rule failure.
symbol_set.boundary: A demerit records a negative mark, but it does not erase the entire value of the person.

clean_separation.⌬: identity = who or what this marks

distortion_tests.name: Category Boundary Test
distortion_tests.question: Is the mark being kept inside its assigned category?

distortion_tests.name: Proof Inflation Test
distortion_tests.question: Is someone treating the mark as proof of more than it actually proves?

distortion_tests.name: Identity Collapse Test
distortion_tests.question: Is a mark of identity being falsely treated as ownership, authority, guilt, destiny, or total personhood?

distortion_tests.name: Honour Versus Valour Test
distortion_tests.question: Is general respect being confused with courage under danger?

distortion_tests.name: Demerit Scope Test
distortion_tests.question: Is a negative mark being inflated into total worthlessness?

failure_modes.name: Mark Literalization
failure_modes.description: Treating the symbol as literal proof instead of a category marker.

failure_modes.name: Identity Overreach
failure_modes.description: Using a mark of identity to claim ownership, authority, guilt, or total definition of a person.

failure_modes.name: Honour Inflation
failure_modes.description: Treating honour as superiority rather than recognition.

failure_modes.name: Distinction Moralization
failure_modes.description: Treating distinction as proof of moral goodness instead of difference or excellence.

failure_modes.name: Demerit Totalization
failure_modes.description: Treating a demerit as if it erases the person's entire value.

one_line_translation: ❖ is honour, ✷ is distinction, ⟁ is valour, ⌬ is identity, and ⛝ is a demerit.
